findings.observed: Exactly five words are present: Vorbereiten, Untersuchen, Auswerten, qualitativ, quantitativ. All are correctly spelled and reliably readable at the actual360x203 preview. findings.criterion: Laboratory eye protection and visible safety
findings.observed: All four person depictions wear transparent wrap-around splash goggles with visible sides/straps and lab coats: preparation, flame test, quantitative measurement and recording. The flame is on a stable bench, the hand is separated from it by a long implement, the burette is upright and clamped over a receiving flask. No visible unsafe hand-to-flame contact or unprotected eyes remain.
findings.limit: A cartoon orientation scene is not a full practical protocol, PPE certification, risk assessment or observation of an actual learner.

findings.observed: A tilted sample vessel pours through a filter-paper/funnel arrangement into a receiving flask; mortar/pestle provide a distinct preparation cue. The qualitative panel has flame/test-tube examples. The quantitative panel has a balance and an upright supported burette with stopcock above an Erlenmeyer flask. These are recognizable method illustrations, not measurement data or a claim that every depicted method fits every unknown sample.

Unlabelled coloured test tubes and simple notebook/grid marks represent observations compared with reference patterns. There is no named substance, NaCl jar, Na+/Fe3+ label, concentration, mass or volume conclusion. The arrows express preparation→investigation→evaluation. They no longer claim identification of a particular compound from unspecific evidence.
findings.limit: The image neither proves identification nor supplies an assessment solution; sufficient independent evidence, controls and uncertainty still belong to actual teaching/practical work.

findings.observed: The recorder is behind the open notebook on the bench, with one hand holding a pencil against the page and the other stabilizing the book. The binding, turned pages and marks are plausible for the actor. With no observer-oriented microtext, there is no misleading reading direction. The titration actor operates the stopcock and holds the receiving flask in a plausible schematic position.

No technical IDs, watermark, logos or copied worksheet are visible. The exact whole goal and practical operators remain unchanged; this is orientation supporting that goal, not evidence of semantic atomicity or completion.
